title: 해외 여행
intro: 해외 여행은 '가 본 나라·도시 묘사 → 여행 준비 과정 → 여행 중 문제·기억에 남는 일 → 과거와 현재 또는 국내 여행과 비교'로 출제됩니다. 작년 여름휴가 때 회사 입사 동기 Minji와 함께 간 일본 오사카(유니버설 스튜디오, 도톤보리 길거리 음식) 이야기 하나로 대부분의 질문을 해결하세요. 비교 질문에는 대학 때의 첫 해외여행을 과거 이야기로, '연차 내고 떠나는 직장인 여행'을 현재 이야기로 쓰면 됩니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Okay, let me tell you about ~) → 언제·어디·누구와 → 거기서 한 일·먹은 음식 세부 → 느낌·좋았던 이유 → 마무리 문장(Yeah, that's ~)
도시는 오사카 하나로 고정: 작년 여름휴가, 동료 Minji, 유니버설 스튜디오, 도톤보리 타코야키. 묘사·경험·비교에 같은 장면을 재활용하세요.
문제 경험 질문은 '무슨 일 → 당황한 감정 → 해결 방법 → 배운 점' 4단계로 말하면 IH 이상 구조가 됩니다.
비교 질문은 대학 때 첫 해외여행(과거: 종이 지도·현금·싼 호스텔) vs 지금(직장인: 앱·카드·짧은 휴가)으로 나누고 used to / these days 를 쓰세요.

expressions.ko: 좋아요, 제 오사카 여행에 대해 말해 볼게요.

expressions.en: I went there last summer with my coworker Minji.
expressions.ko: 작년 여름에 회사 동료 Minji랑 거기 갔어요.

expressions.en: The flight was only about an hour and a half.
expressions.ko: 비행시간이 한 시간 반 정도밖에 안 됐어요.

expressions.en: I used my summer vacation days.
We tried a lot of street food.
expressions.ko: 길거리 음식을 정말 많이 먹어 봤어요.

expressions.en: We got on the wrong train.
expressions.note: get on the wrong ~ : ~을 잘못 타다

expressions.en: We booked the flight two months early.
expressions.ko: 우리는 두 달 일찍 비행기를 예약했어요.

expressions.en: My phone battery was almost dead.

expressions.note: 문제 상황 경험 답변 필수 표현

The food alone was worth the trip.
It turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
expressions.note: turn out to be ~ : 결국 ~로 밝혀지다

expressions.en: So yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far.
expressions.ko: 그래서 오사카가 지금까지 제일 좋아하는 도시예요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like to travel abroad. Tell me about a country or city you have visited and really liked. What was it like, and what did you enjoy doing there?
questions.ko: 설문에서 해외 여행을 좋아한다고 하셨습니다. 가 본 나라나 도시 중 정말 좋았던 곳에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떤 곳이었고, 거기서 무엇을 즐겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 도시 이름·언제·누구와 → 도시 분위기 묘사 → 즐긴 것(유니버설 스튜디오, 도톤보리 음식) → 'So yeah, that's why ~' 마무리
'서울처럼 크고 바쁘지만 사람들이 더 여유로워 보였다'처럼 서울과 짧게 비교하면 묘사가 생생해져요.
Minji와 함께 간 이야기로 고정하면 경험·비교 질문에서도 같은 장면을 쓸 수 있어요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my trip to Osaka. Osaka is a big city in Japan. I went there last summer with my coworker Minji. The flight was only about an hour and a half. Osaka is busy like Seoul, but the people were really friendly. We went to Universal Studios. The lines were really long, but the rides were so fun. At night, we walked around Dotonbori and tried a lot of street food. So yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about a city I really liked. It's Osaka in Japan. I went there last summer with my coworker Minji. We joined the company at the same time, so we're really close. We used our summer vacation days and stayed for four days. The flight from Seoul was only about an hour and a half, so it was really easy. Osaka is a lot like Seoul because it's big and busy, but the people there seemed more relaxed and friendly. The highlight was Universal Studios. The lines were really long and it was super hot, but the rides were amazing, and we screamed the whole time. At night, we walked around Dotonbori, which is a famous street full of bright signs and food stalls. We tried takoyaki and okonomiyaki. Honestly, the food alone was worth the trip. So yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. The city I liked the most is definitely Osaka in Japan. I went there last summer with my coworker Minji. We started at the company on the same day, so we've been through a lot together, and we'd been talking about a trip for ages. We finally used our summer vacation days and went for four days. The flight was only about an hour and a half, so it felt like we were there before we even finished our snacks. Osaka is kind of like Seoul because it's big and busy, but the vibe is totally different. People seemed more laid-back, and everyone was super friendly, even when we couldn't speak Japanese. We spent one whole day at Universal Studios. It was boiling hot and the lines were crazy long, but once we got on the rides, we forgot all about it and screamed like little kids. My favorite part, though, was Dotonbori at night. The whole street was covered in bright neon signs, and there were food stalls everywhere. We tried takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and fried skewers, and honestly, the food alone was worth the trip. For once, I didn't think about work at all. So yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far.

questions.en: What do you usually do to prepare for a trip abroad? Tell me about all the steps you take, from booking the trip to packing your bags.
questions.ko: 해외 여행을 가기 전에 보통 무엇을 준비하나요? 여행 예약부터 짐 싸기까지 거치는 모든 단계를 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 휴가 날짜 정하기(팀장님께 휴가 신청) → 항공·숙소 예약 → 일정·맛집 찾기 → 환전·데이터 → 짐 싸기 → 마무리 문장
First, Then, After that, A day or two before, Finally 순서 표현으로 단계를 나눠 말하세요.
'떠나기 전 업무 인수인계'처럼 직장인다운 단계를 하나 넣으면 답변이 자연스러워요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about how I prepare for a trip abroad. First, I pick my vacation dates and tell my team leader. Then, I book the flight and the hotel online. I usually book two months early because it's cheaper. After that, I look for good places to eat. I also buy a data plan for my phone. A day before the trip, I pack my suitcase. I always double-check my passport. Yeah, that's how I prepare for a trip abroad.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about how I get ready for a trip abroad. Since I work at an IT company, the first step is always picking my vacation dates. I check my team's schedule and ask my team leader for the days off. Then, my friend Minji and I book the flight and the hotel. We try to book at least two months early, because prices go up really fast. After that, my job is to make a list of places to go and things to eat. Before our trip to Osaka, I watched a lot of travel videos and found the best takoyaki places. I also buy a data plan online, so I can use maps there. A day or two before we leave, I pack my suitcase. I always bring comfortable shoes, a power adapter, and some medicine just in case. And of course, I double-check my passport the night before. So yeah, that's pretty much how I prepare for a trip abroad.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. As an office worker, preparing for a trip abroad actually starts way before I book anything. The first thing I do is look at my team's calendar and find a week when there are no big campaigns going on. Then I ask my team leader for the days off, usually two or three months in advance. Once that's settled, my coworker Minji and I book our flight and hotel. We've learned the hard way that prices shoot up if you wait too long, so we book as early as we can. After that, we split up the planning. Minji is in charge of shopping, and I'm in charge of food, which is kind of my specialty. Before our Osaka trip, I watched tons of travel videos and saved a list of takoyaki places on my map app. I also buy a data plan online and put a little cash in my wallet, although I mostly use my card these days. About a week before I leave, I hand over my work to another teammate so nobody has to call me on vacation. Finally, I pack the night before. Comfortable shoes, a power adapter, and some medicine just in case. And I always double-check my passport, like, three times. Yeah, that's how I prepare for a trip abroad.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem or an unexpected situation while traveling abroad? Tell me about that experience in detail. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
questions.ko: 해외 여행 중에 문제가 생기거나 예상치 못한 상황을 겪은 적이 있나요? 그 경험을 자세히 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떻게 해결했나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·어디서 → 무슨 문제가 생겼는지 → 당황한 감정 → 어떻게 해결했는지 → 배운 점 + 마무리 문장
All of a sudden, To make things worse, Luckily, In the end 같은 이야기 연결어로 긴장감을 만드세요.
오사카에서 Minji와 지하철을 잘못 타고 배터리가 꺼진 이야기로 고정하면 준비가 쉬워요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem abroad? Let me think. Last summer, I went to Osaka with my coworker Minji. One evening, we got on the wrong train. We didn't know where we were. My phone battery was almost dead, so I couldn't use the map. I was really nervous. Luckily, a station worker helped us. He wrote down the right train for us. We got back to the hotel an hour late. Yeah, that's the problem I had abroad.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. Last summer, I went to Osaka with my coworker Minji, and something stressful happened. One evening, we went shopping and wanted to go back to our hotel. The subway system in Osaka is really complicated, and we got on the wrong train. All of a sudden, we were in a part of the city we didn't recognize at all. To make things worse, my phone battery was almost dead, and Minji's phone didn't have data. I was really nervous, but I tried to stay calm. Luckily, we found a station worker. We couldn't speak Japanese, so I just showed him our hotel name. He was so kind and wrote down the train and the stop for us. In the end, we got back safely, just an hour late. Now I always carry a portable charger. Yeah, that's the most stressful moment I've had abroad.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem while traveling? Yeah, I definitely have a story. Last summer, I went to Osaka with my coworker Minji. On our third night, we went shopping and stayed out pretty late. When we tried to head back to our hotel, we hopped on what we thought was the right train. But after a few stops, nothing looked familiar, and the station names didn't match our route at all. We had gotten on an express train going in the totally wrong direction. To make things worse, my phone battery was at two percent, and Minji's data wasn't working. I'm usually the calm one at work, but honestly, I was panicking inside. We got off at the next station and found a station worker. Neither of us could speak Japanese, so I just showed him our hotel's name on a receipt. He not only wrote down the right train and stop for us, but he actually walked us to the platform. I was so touched. We finally got back an hour and a half late, totally exhausted, but we couldn't stop laughing about it. It turned out to be a blessing in disguise, because now it's our favorite story to tell at the office. And these days, I never travel without a portable charger. Yeah, that's the craziest thing that's happened to me abroad.

questions.en: How is the way you travel abroad now different from the first time you traveled overseas? Or, how does traveling abroad compare to traveling within Korea?
questions.ko: 지금 해외 여행하는 방식은 처음 해외여행을 갔을 때와 어떻게 다른가요? 또는 해외 여행은 국내 여행과 비교해 어떤가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 처음 해외여행(대학 때, 긴장·종이 지도·현금·싼 호스텔) → 지금(직장인: 앱·카드·짧은 휴가·좋은 호텔) → 느낌·어느 쪽이 좋은지 → 마무리 문장
Back then / used to 와 These days / now 로 과거와 현재를 분명히 나누세요.
국내 여행 비교가 나오면 '부산은 주말에 쉽게, 오사카는 연차를 길게 써야 함'으로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about how my trips abroad have changed. My first trip abroad was in college. I went with my college friends. Back then, I was really nervous because everything was new. We used a paper map and carried a lot of cash. We stayed in a cheap hostel. These days, I use map apps and pay with my card. But I'm busy at work, so my trips are short. Yeah, that's how my trips abroad have changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. My first trip abroad was in college, and it was really different from how I travel now. I went with two friends during winter break. Back then, I was really nervous because everything was new. I didn't even know how to check in at the airport. We also had to exchange a lot of cash and carry a paper map. Since we were students, we stayed in a cheap hostel and ate convenience store food a lot. These days, things are much easier. When I went to Osaka with my coworker Minji last summer, I used a map app to find the subway, and I paid for almost everything with my card. We also stayed in a nice hotel. The only downside is that I can't take long vacations anymore. So yeah, that's pretty much how my trips abroad have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's an interesting question. Let me think. My first trip abroad was back in college, and looking back, it was a completely different experience. I went with two friends during winter break, and I was so nervous that I barely slept the night before. I didn't even know how to check in at the airport, so I just followed my friends around like a lost puppy. We used to carry paper maps and a big envelope of cash, and we stayed in the cheapest hostel we could find. We lived on convenience store sandwiches to save money, but honestly, it felt like a huge adventure. These days, I travel in a totally different way. Now that I have a steady job, I can afford a nice hotel and good restaurants. When Minji and I went to Osaka last summer, I used a map app for the subway, a translation app to order food, and my card for almost everything. It's so much more comfortable. But there's a catch. Back in college, I had weeks of vacation, and now I have to squeeze a trip into four or five days off. If I had to choose, I'd still pick traveling now, because I'm more confident. So yeah, that's how my trips abroad have changed.

pronunciation.tip: 두 번째 음절 '브로-'에 강세. 첫 a는 약하게 '어'로 흘려요.
첫 음절 '패'에 강세. 끝 t는 살짝 끊듯이 약하게.
'수트케이스'. suit의 t는 거의 들리지 않게 멈추듯 발음해요.
두 번째 음절 '케이'에 강세. v는 윗니를 아랫입술에 대고 '브'가 아닌 진동 소리로.
미국식은 '스케줄', s 다음에 k 소리를 분명히 내세요.

patterns.en: It has a lively atmosphere that makes me feel excited.
patterns.ko: 그곳은 활기찬 분위기가 있어서 저를 신나게 해요.

patterns.en: I have a friend named Minji, and we went to Osaka together last summer.
patterns.ko: 저에게는 민지라는 친구가 있는데, 작년 여름에 같이 오사카에 갔어요.

patterns.en: First, I ask my team leader for the days off. Then, I book the flight and the hotel.
patterns.ko: 먼저 팀장님께 휴가를 신청해요. 그다음 항공권과 호텔을 예약해요.

patterns.ko: 민지와 제가 오사카에서 지하철을 잘못 탔을 때 예상치 못한 일이 일어났어요.

patterns.en: It turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
Since then, I always make sure to bring a portable charger.
patterns.ko: 그 이후로 저는 항상 보조배터리를 꼭 챙겨요.

patterns.en: Compared to my first trip abroad, traveling now is much more comfortable.
patterns.ko: 처음 해외여행을 갔을 때와 비교하면, 지금 여행하는 게 훨씬 더 편해요.
